source_evidence.observation: The paper defines matrix absolute value componentwise by |A| = (|a_ij|), and uses fl_p on a matrix expression to mean evaluation at a specified precision followed by rounding to precision p.

source_evidence.anchor: section 2.1, mixed precision block FMA definition
source_evidence.observation: A block FMA has A in R^(b1 x b), B in R^(b x b2), and C in R^(b1 x b2); A and B are supplied in precision u_low, while C and the returned D may use u_low or u_high. Its mathematical operation is D = C + AB.

The FMA output unit roundoff u_FMA is either u_low or u_high. The expression C+AB is computed internally at unit roundoff u_bar <= u_FMA and then, when needed, rounded to u_FMA. The standard model is fl(a op b) = (a op b)(1+delta), |delta| <= u, with the equivalent reciprocal form in (2.4).
The paper defines gamma_k = ku/(1-ku), assumes ku < 1 for every relevant k and precision, and specifies that accents and the superscript FMA on gamma are inherited by its underlying unit roundoff.

Algorithm 3.1 partitions A in R^(m x n) into b1 x b blocks and B in R^(n x t) into b x b2 blocks, with p=m/b1, q=n/b, and r=t/b2 integers. It converts A and B to u_low if necessary, initializes each C_ij to zero, chains q block FMAs, and rounds the resulting block to output precision u when u differs from u_FMA.

The inputs are not required to have been supplied in u_low. The paper notes that scaling may be needed to avoid underflow or overflow and explicitly assumes throughout this analysis that neither occurs.

For a scalar entry, the q-block chain uses s_0=0 and s_i=s_(i-1)+sum from j=(i-1)b+1 through ib of x_j y_j. The effective rounding unit is u_tilde_FMA=u if u>u_FMA; otherwise it is 0 if u_bar>=u_FMA and u_FMA if u_bar<u_FMA. The first branch has explicit priority when conditions overlap.

The scalar forward error is bounded by (gamma_tilde_FMA(q)+gamma_bar(n)+gamma_tilde_FMA(q)gamma_bar(n))|x|^T|y|. The derivation starts with left-to-right evaluation, but the paper says this bound is valid for all evaluation orders; right-to-left blocked summation permits gamma_bar(n) to be replaced by gamma_bar(q+b-1).

For inputs not already in u_low, A_tilde=fl_low(A)=A+Delta A and B_tilde=fl_low(B)=B+Delta B, with |Delta A|<=u_low|A| and |Delta B|<=u_low|B|. Applying the low-input bound to A_tilde B_tilde and expanding produces C_hat=AB+Delta A B+A Delta B+Delta A Delta B+Delta C.

For C=AB with A in R^(m x n) and B in R^(n x t), not necessarily supplied in u_low, Algorithm 3.1 with q=n/b produces C_hat satisfying |C-C_hat| <= (2u_low+u_low^2+(gamma_tilde_FMA(q)+gamma_bar(n)+gamma_tilde_FMA(q)gamma_bar(n))(1+u_low)^2)|A||B|.

binders: [Explicit in Theorem 3.2] A in R^(m x n) and B in R^(n x t), with exact mathematical product C=AB and computed output C_hat. (Evidence: PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)".)

[Inherited from Algorithm 3.1] Matrix and block dimensions m,n,t,b1,b,b2 satisfy p=m/b1, q=n/b, and r=t/b2 with p,q,r integers. (Evidence: PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor "Algorithm 3.1 and rectangular block partition".)

[Inherited precision parameters] u_low and u_high are unit roundoffs; u_FMA is the block-FMA output unit roundoff, u_bar is its internal evaluation unit roundoff, u is Algorithm 3.1's output unit roundoff, and u_tilde_FMA is the effective chain-rounding unit defined by (3.3). (Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor "equations (2.3)-(2.6) and gamma notation"; PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor "equations (3.1)-(3.3), effective FMA rounding precision".)
hypotheses: [Explicit] The exact operands are conformable real matrices A in R^(m x n) and B in R^(n x t); they need not initially be supplied in precision u_low. (Evidence: PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)".)

[Inherited] The product is evaluated specifically by Algorithm 3.1 using the stated rectangular partition and q=n/b chained block FMAs per output block. (Evidence: PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor "Algorithm 3.1 and rectangular block partition".)

[Inherited] Inputs are rounded to u_low when necessary, with componentwise conversion errors bounded by u_low times the corresponding componentwise absolute value. (Evidence: PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "input-conversion equations preceding Theorem 3.2".)

[Standing arithmetic model] Floating-point operations satisfy the relative-error model (2.3), equivalently (2.4), and all relevant gamma denominators are positive because ku<1 is assumed. (Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor "equations (2.3)-(2.6) and gamma notation" and "gamma definition following equation (2.4)".)
[Standing exceptional-value assumption] Underflow and overflow do not occur. (Evidence: PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor "paragraph following Algorithm 3.1".)
conclusions: [Equation (3.6)] |C-C_hat| <= (2u_low + u_low^2 + (gamma_tilde_FMA(q) + gamma_bar(n) + gamma_tilde_FMA(q)gamma_bar(n))(1+u_low)^2)|A||B|, componentwise. Here gamma_bar(n)=n*u_bar/(1-n*u_bar) and gamma_tilde_FMA(q)=q*u_tilde_FMA/(1-q*u_tilde_FMA). (Evidence: PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)"; PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor "gamma definition following equation (2.4)".)
definitions_and_conventions: [Explicit convention] |A| means the matrix whose ij entry is |a_ij|. (Evidence: PDF p. 3, printed C126, anchor "componentwise absolute-value convention".)

[Explicit convention] fl_p applied to a matrix expression means that the expression is evaluated at a specified precision, possibly different from p, and then rounded to precision p. (Evidence: PDF p. 3, printed C126, anchor "componentwise absolute-value convention".)

[Explicit definition] gamma_k=ku/(1-ku); an accent or FMA superscript on gamma applies to the underlying u as well. Thus gamma_bar(n)=n*u_bar/(1-n*u_bar), and gamma_tilde_FMA(q)=q*u_tilde_FMA/(1-q*u_tilde_FMA). (Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor "gamma definition following equation (2.4)".)
[Explicit conversion notation] A_tilde=fl_low(A)=A+Delta A and B_tilde=fl_low(B)=B+Delta B. (Evidence: PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "input-conversion equations preceding Theorem 3.2".)

[Inferred from standard matrix notation, supported by the scalar form] |A||B| is ordinary matrix multiplication of the nonnegative componentwise-absolute matrices, not entrywise multiplication. (Evidence: PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor "equation (3.4) and evaluation-order paragraph"; PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)".)
implicit_context: [Inherited from Algorithm 3.1] Divisibility of m by b1, n by b, and t by b2 is required; Theorem 3.2 itself only repeats q=n/b. (Evidence: PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor "Algorithm 3.1 and rectangular block partition"; PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)".)

[Inherited from the block-FMA framework] u_FMA is either u_low or u_high, and C+AB is internally evaluated at u_bar<=u_FMA before any required output rounding. (Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor "equations (2.3)-(2.6) and gamma notation".)

[Inherited from the scalar analysis] The displayed gamma_bar(n) bound remains valid for all evaluation orders, although the derivation first describes left-to-right evaluation. (Evidence: PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor "equation (3.4) and evaluation-order paragraph".)

[Cross-referenced derivation] Theorem 3.2 applies the low-input Algorithm 3.1 error bound to A_tilde B_tilde and then adds and bounds both input-conversion errors and their product. (Evidence: PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "input-conversion equations preceding Theorem 3.2".)
statement.algorithm_linkage: The selected result is for Algorithm 3.1, not arbitrary matrix multiplication: round A and B to u_low if necessary; for each b1 x b2 output block initialize C_ij=0; for ell=1,...,q update C_ij with C_ij+A_tilde_(i,ell)B_tilde_(ell,j) using a block FMA whose output precision is u_FMA; after the chain, round to output precision u when u differs from u_FMA. (Evidence: PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor "Algorithm 3.1 and rectangular block partition".)
numerical_model: Each basic operation uses fl(a op b)=(a op b)(1+delta), |delta|<=u, or the equivalent reciprocal form, for op in {+,-,multiplication,division}. (Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor "equations (2.3)-(2.6) and gamma notation".)

A block FMA computes C+AB internally at u_bar<=u_FMA and rounds to u_FMA when required; u_FMA is either u_low or u_high. (Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor "equations (2.3)-(2.6) and gamma notation".)
Initial conversions obey |Delta A|<=u_low|A| and |Delta B|<=u_low|B| componentwise. (Evidence: PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "input-conversion equations preceding Theorem 3.2".)

The effective chain-rounding unit is u_tilde_FMA=u when u>u_FMA; otherwise it is 0 when u_bar>=u_FMA and u_FMA when u_bar<u_FMA, with the first branch taking priority. (Evidence: PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor "equations (3.1)-(3.3), effective FMA rounding precision".)

When u>u_FMA>u_bar would cause two roundings, the analysis deliberately includes only one rounding. (Evidence: PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor "equations (3.1)-(3.3), effective FMA rounding precision".)
error_notions: The result is a componentwise absolute forward-error bound comparing the exact product C=AB with the computed C_hat. (Evidence: PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)".)
The theorem does not state a normwise, relative-error, or backward-error conclusion. (Evidence: PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)".)
Input rounding is also controlled componentwise through |Delta A| and |Delta B|. (Evidence: PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "input-conversion equations preceding Theorem 3.2".)
norms: No matrix or vector norm appears in Theorem 3.2. (Evidence: PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)".)

Absolute-value bars on matrices denote componentwise absolute value, and the inequality is componentwise. (Evidence: PDF p. 3, printed C126, anchor "componentwise absolute-value convention"; PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)".)

The scalar precursor uses |x|^T|y|, confirming that the matrix factor |A||B| aggregates absolute products over the shared dimension. (Evidence: PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor "equation (3.4) and evaluation-order paragraph".)
constants_and_indexing: The shared dimension is divided into q=n/b blocks, with no floor or ceiling; q is an integer inherited from Algorithm 3.1. (Evidence: PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor "Algorithm 3.1 and rectangular block partition"; PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)".)
The conversion contribution is exactly 2u_low+u_low^2. (Evidence: PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)".)
The arithmetic contribution is exactly (gamma_tilde_FMA(q)+gamma_bar(n)+gamma_tilde_FMA(q)gamma_bar(n))(1+u_low)^2. (Evidence: PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)".)

The scalar chain indexes block i from 1 through q and entries of block i from (i-1)b+1 through ib. Because s_0=0, the first block uses b rather than b+1 in the theta factor multiplying x_1y_1. (Evidence: PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor "equations (3.1)-(3.3), effective FMA rounding precision".)

For right-to-left blocked summation, gamma_bar(n) may be sharpened to gamma_bar(q+b-1), but equation (3.6) retains gamma_bar(n). (Evidence: PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor "equation (3.4) and evaluation-order paragraph"; PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)".)
higher_order_terms: Within the stated single-rounding model, equation (3.6) is not merely first order: it retains u_low^2, the product gamma_tilde_FMA(q)gamma_bar(n), and the full factor (1+u_low)^2. (Evidence: PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)".)
Equation (3.6) contains no big-O remainder. (Evidence: PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)".)

Separately, the general model notes that setting u_bar=0 represents a rounded exact block result only to within O(u_FMA^2), because |D_hat| rather than |D| occurs on the right of (2.6). (Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor "equations (2.3)-(2.6) and gamma notation".)

The effect of an actual two-stage rounding when u>u_FMA>u_bar is omitted rather than represented by an explicit remainder term. (Evidence: PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor "equations (3.1)-(3.3), effective FMA rounding precision".)
exceptional_values: The analysis explicitly assumes that underflow and overflow do not occur. (Evidence: PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor "paragraph following Algorithm 3.1".)
The paper notes that scaling may be necessary in Algorithm 3.1 to avoid underflow or overflow. (Evidence: PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor "paragraph following Algorithm 3.1".)

The cited theorem and numerical-model passages do not specify behavior for NaNs, infinities, subnormal arithmetic, or other exceptional-value semantics beyond excluding underflow and overflow. (Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor "equations (2.3)-(2.6) and gamma notation"; PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor "paragraph following Algorithm 3.1".)

undebatable_constraints: The conclusion must reproduce the complete coefficient 2u_low+u_low^2+(gamma_tilde_FMA(q)+gamma_bar(n)+gamma_tilde_FMA(q)gamma_bar(n))(1+u_low)^2. (Evidence: PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)".)
The result concerns the exact real product C=AB and the Algorithm 3.1 output C_hat for A in R^(m x n) and B in R^(n x t). (Evidence: PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)".)

A and B must not be required to be supplied in u_low; the theorem explicitly allows otherwise and accounts for conversion. (Evidence: PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)" and "input-conversion equations preceding Theorem 3.2".)

The bound is componentwise and uses componentwise matrix absolute values, not a norm. (Evidence: PDF p. 3, printed C126, anchor "componentwise absolute-value convention"; PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)".)
The shared dimension must satisfy q=n/b under Algorithm 3.1's integer block partition. (Evidence: PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor "Algorithm 3.1 and rectangular block partition".)

gamma_bar(n) and gamma_tilde_FMA(q) must be tied respectively to u_bar and the piecewise effective unit u_tilde_FMA, with gamma_k=ku/(1-ku). (Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor "gamma definition following equation (2.4)"; PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor "equations (3.1)-(3.3), effective FMA rounding precision".)

The assumptions ku<1 for relevant indices and precisions and absence of underflow and overflow are inherited by the theorem. (Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor "gamma definition following equation (2.4)"; PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor "paragraph following Algorithm 3.1".)

The factors u_low^2, gamma_tilde_FMA(q)gamma_bar(n), and (1+u_low)^2 cannot be discarded as higher-order terms when reproducing equation (3.6). (Evidence: PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)".)

The selected algorithm is the chained rectangular block-FMA multiplication with initial low-precision conversions and final output precision u. (Evidence: PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor "Algorithm 3.1 and rectangular block partition".)

ambiguities.issue: The theorem does not fix a single source storage precision for A and B.
ambiguities.evidence: Theorem 3.2 says that A and B are "not necessarily given in precision u_low," while the Algorithm 3.1 discussion gives u_high only as an example and converts inputs to u_low if necessary. (PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor "paragraph following Algorithm 3.1"; PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)".)
ambiguities.impact: A formal contract must not add either an already-u_low hypothesis or a specifically-u_high hypothesis; it must retain the modeled conversion errors.

ambiguities.issue: The treatment of two successive roundings is intentionally approximate.
ambiguities.evidence: For u>u_FMA>u_bar the paper says two roundings are needed but includes only a single rounding in the analysis, describing the effect as negligible without giving an explicit correction in (3.6). (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor "equations (3.1)-(3.3), effective FMA rounding precision".)
ambiguities.impact: Equation (3.6) should be represented as the paper's stated single-rounding-model bound, not as an exact accounting of both physical roundings.

ambiguities.issue: Algorithm 3.1 does not mandate one arithmetic evaluation order for every implementation.
ambiguities.evidence: The scalar derivation begins with left-to-right evaluation, then states that (3.4) is valid for all evaluation orders and gives gamma_bar(q+b-1) as a sharper replacement under right-to-left blocked summation. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor "equation (3.4) and evaluation-order paragraph".)
ambiguities.impact: The displayed Theorem 3.2 contract must keep gamma_bar(n); the sharper indexed constant is conditional on the right-to-left variant.

ambiguities.issue: Exceptional-value behavior beyond underflow and overflow is not specified.
ambiguities.evidence: The paper explicitly excludes underflow and overflow but the cited model and theorem passages do not discuss NaNs, infinities, signed zeros, or subnormal handling. (PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor "equations (2.3)-(2.6) and gamma notation"; PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor "paragraph following Algorithm 3.1".)
ambiguities.impact: No additional IEEE exceptional-value semantics should be inferred or encoded as part of the source claim.

contract_plain_english: Take conformable real matrices A and B, partition them as Algorithm 3.1 requires, round them to the low input precision when necessary, and compute each output block by chaining q=n/b block FMAs before producing output precision u. (Evidence: PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor "Algorithm 3.1 and rectangular block partition".) Under the paper's relative-error model, valid gamma denominators, and no underflow or overflow, the computed C_hat differs componentwise from the exact AB by at most (2u_low+u_low^2+(gamma_tilde_FMA(q)+gamma_bar(n)+gamma_tilde_FMA(q)gamma_bar(n))(1+u_low)^2)|A||B|. (Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor "gamma definition following equation (2.4)"; PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor "paragraph following Algorithm 3.1"; PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)".) This is a full componentwise forward-error bound, not a normwise, relative, backward, or first-order-only statement. (Evidence: PDF p. 3, printed C126, anchor "componentwise absolute-value convention"; PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor "Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)".)
